entities.name: PMID:25423567
observations: In human granulosa-derived SVOG cells, SNAP induced PTGS2/COX-2 mRNA and protein and increased PGE2; COX-1 was unaffected.
8-bromo-cGMP mimicked SNAP, and CREB knockdown attenuated COX-2 induction and PGE2 production.
The study supports NO/cGMP to CREB to COX-2/PGE2 signaling, but does not establish sGC or PKG causality by direct inhibition or rescue.

entities.name: Nitric oxide
observations: SNAP, an NO donor, induced COX-2/PTGS2 expression and PGE2 production in human granulosa-derived SVOG cells.

entities.name: cGMP
observations: 8-bromo-cGMP mimicked SNAP-induced COX-2 expression and PGE2 production in human granulosa-derived SVOG cells.

entities.name: CREB
observations: SNAP and 8-bromo-cGMP activated CREB signaling; CREB knockdown attenuated COX-2 induction and PGE2 production in SVOG cells.

entities.name: PTGS2
observations: SNAP and 8-bromo-cGMP increased PTGS2/COX-2 expression in human granulosa-derived SVOG cells.

entities.name: Prostaglandin E2
observations: SNAP and 8-bromo-cGMP increased PGE2 production in human granulosa-derived SVOG cells.

entities.name: SVOG cells
observations: Immortalized human granulosa-derived cells from women undergoing IVF were used for the direct mechanistic experiments.

entities.name: PMID:36049621
observations: In human IVF granulosa cells, cigarette-smoke exposure was associated with increased iNOS and COX-2 protein/activity, follicular-fluid PGE2, and pCREB; this was observational and non-causal.

entities.name: Distal renal tubular acidosis
observations: Hypokalemic distal (type 1) RTA can cause weakness, leg pain, flattened T waves, and tachypnea from metabolic acidosis.
Acquired distal RTA is classically associated with Sjögren syndrome; rheumatoid arthritis and SLE are less characteristic associations.

entities.name: Sjögren syndrome
observations: Sjögren syndrome is the strongest classic autoimmune association with distal renal tubular acidosis among the answer choices.

entities.name: Gitelman syndrome
observations: Gitelman syndrome causes inherited hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, making it less consistent with tachypnea suggesting metabolic acidosis.

entities.name: Bartter syndrome
observations: Bartter syndrome causes inherited hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, making it less consistent with tachypnea suggesting metabolic acidosis.
